description: Multi-service selection by header (MCPWARP.md §4.8 step 1): one connection holds a-svc and b-svc, both active. The request carries X-Mcpwarp-Server-Id (here in upper case: header names match case-insensitively) equal to b-svc's registered id, so b-svc's handler serves it even though its Host names a-svc: the header, when present, decides alone and the Host label is not consulted. The application still sees the request unchanged, Host and both X-Mcpwarp-* headers included. Header selection is opt-in: the runner MUST enable the SDK option trustServerIdHeader (default off, under which the Host label alone selects and this request would go to a-svc); a runner that cannot skips the fixture with a note (runnerRequirement).
in:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: a-svc-alice.tunnel.example
accept: application/json, text/event-stream
content-type: application/json
X-MCPWARP-SERVER-ID: 4f1d2c3b-0a1e-4c5d-9e8f-00000000000b
X-Mcpwarp-Server-Name: b-svc
user-agent: Go-http-client/1.1
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
out:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

28
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
0
notes: The runner registers both services on one connection with registered.services[] = services[] (name, id, url), gives each its own instance of the handler, writes `in` on a stream and checks that only routedTo's instance was called. An edge that sets the header never sends one that disagrees with Host; the disagreement only proves the precedence. An id that matches no held service is 503 service unavailable, with no fallback to the Host label.
